newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty slightly softer, seen stable in recent range.
newsitem.headline: Zloty slightly softer, seen stable in recent range.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed slightly softer at around 1.2 percent weaker than the parity rate after early slip on a domestic order and ensuing speculation and is seen stable in its recent band, dealers said.
"After the first half an hour of larger moves the zloty stabilized and was trading sideways," said Marek Cherubin, forex dealer at Bank Creditanstals SA in Warsaw.

Dealers said the zloty would remain within its recent range between minus 1.0 percent and minus 1.5 percent from parity in the near-term as foreign players are largely absent from the market ahead of the September 21 parliamentary polls.

"The central bank showed it would not allow the zloty to firm above parity, while possibly higher inflation, slower GDP growth and September's parliamentary polls all push the zloty down," said Adam Roeske, forex dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
The zloty closed at 1.12/1.19 percent weaker than the trading band centre, vs Monday's minus 1.04/1.13 percent.
It ended at 3.4875/00 to the dollar, against 3.4700/30 on Monday and at 1.8995/10 to the mark, against 1.9060/80.
On the money market overnight rates rates rose by 0.3 to 0.4 points 21.60/22.60 percent while tomorrow/next rates closed at 21.80/22.20 percent.

The one-day rate rise followed the National Bank of Poland's drainage of 1.42 billion zlotys from the system through a seven- and 14-day reverse repo operation at unchanged maximum rates of 23.45 and 23.55 percent respectively.
Dealers said the drainage may prompt the rates to go further up to around 22.10 or 22.20 at offer for overnight rates on Wednesday.
